summary: The first fully verified 660-frame projection made known source and accepted flower pixels exact by construction, but review of the metrics found that the color-only skin negative removed too much of the tracked flower layer.
evidence: The run encoded and verified 660 frames in 15.2708 seconds at 43.2199 projection FPS.
Known-source exactness, flower MAD, and flower temporal residual all reached their exact pre-encode gates.
Only 942140 restore pixels survived from 4213773 tracked flower pixels inside the edit support because the unconstrained skin proxy classified broad warm scene regions.
lessons: Occlusion negatives must be the intersection of skin evidence with explicit source-hand tracks, not a scene-wide color decision.
limitations: The run is not promoted because the broad negative could leave generated flower pixels inside the edit support.
next_actions: Constrain skin negatives with the 660-frame source-hand coordinate track and rerun in a fresh directory.
